name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 6 points on the PVI
Incumbent Bill Foster has a large cash advantage ($2.5M vs $23K)
Prediction markets price Foster at 96% to win
model.rationale: Foster combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, and an overwhelming financial edge over Jeff Walter, whose campaign has almost no cash on hand. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, so the forecast stays at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing a tighter race would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a district that leans Democratic by about six points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.5 million on hand after raising over $2.1 million, while Republican Jeff Walter has raised about $311 thousand and reports only about $23 thousand in cash. No outside groups are spending against Foster, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

With no public general-election polling, the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Foster's chances at about 96 percent. The combination of incumbency, the district's partisan lean, and the stark fundraising gap points to a safe Democratic hold, with Foster favored by roughly nineteen points.
